Issued at 340 AM EDT Mon Oct 12 2026

===== Foggy Morning Now But Heat Returns Today =====

We can finally say that the remnants of Isaias are getting kicked 
out to the east coast. Unfortunately, left over residual moisture at 
the surface combined with clear skies overhead have allowed 
widespread dense fog to form, at least throughout central, eastern 
and southern KY. A Dense Fog Advisory has been issued for most of 
our KY counties as a result and may be expanded for the morning rush 
hour. Visibilities have dropped to 1/4 mile in places, with less 
prevalent fog in Indiana. Even here though, the usual valley 
locations near creeks and streams have formed thick fog. Regardless, 
allow extra time to go to work today and increase the following 
distance. This is probably said too much but never let your guard 
down driving foggy roadways.

Good news is that mostly clear to partly cloudy skies are expected 
today. A very weak mid-high level disturbance will drift high to mid 
level clouds in the late morning and afternoon hours from west to 
east. As they drift, they'll allow western areas to receive more 
peak heating from direct sunlight in the afternoon with highs 
reaching the upper 80s with low 80s in the east due to the timing of 
the passing clouds. There is a low-end chance (<20%) of some western 
communities to reach 90 degrees today. Those that don't see 90 today 
will have a higher chance tomorrow. Before then, SW flow will remain 
as ridging builds in today and Tuesday with lows Tuesday morning in 
the low 60s. With good mixing today, fog probabilities are near zero 
or at least well below 20% Tuesday morning.

For Tuesday, highs are quick to jump into the mid to upper 80s 
across the entire CWA. SW flow may be a little stronger in western 
communities with some communities well west of I-65 having a 40-50% 
of reaching 90 Tuesday, which is quite warm for mid-October. Tuesday 
ends quietly like today will be with warm overnight lows in the low 
to upper 60s.

===== Rain Returns with Major Cool Down by the Weekend =====

As Wednesday arrives, a pattern shift will be ongoing. A battle of 
influence between a retreating high to our south and a slowly 
advancing trough trying to lift north at the same time arrives on 
Wednesday afternoon. Long range models are painting a picture of the 
advancing trough slowly pushing east being slowed down. A NE 
oriented jet streak on the east side of the trough encourages the 
trough to lift north over the northern Ohio Valley. However, this 
jet streak may be close enough for our CWA to receive repeated waves 
of rain from decaying MCVs and moisture streaming from the Pacific 
and Gulf. At this time, it's difficult to determine which passing 
disturbance will deposit the most rain. However, latest LREF 
guidance shows PWATs exceeding the 99th percentile of climatology 
near 2.00" in our Indiana counties and slightly south of the Ohio. 
With how warm we will be in the mid to upper 80s, any rain that 
approaches brings the threat of storms. However, the best shear will 
remain too far north as the jet streak seems pointed towards the 
Great Lakes. Additionally, instability seems to be rather weak 
though enough will be around for at least some rumbles of thunder.

As this trough slowly trudges east, energy will be transferred to a 
developing low somewhere near the Great Lakes, possibly aided with 
extra lift from the left exit region of the aforementioned jet 
streak. High temperatures are generally slow to cool as the trough 
will take a while to clear. The exception to this would be quick-
timed rain-cooled afternoons from passing MCVs. The trough should 
clear by Friday as a mostly dry cold front passes through. 

With all that said, rainfall totals this week are right-skewed with 
the highest totals from LREF ranging 1-3". The consensus is near 0.5-
1", though I'd imagine localized areas of 1-3" are possible should 
convection come and go for a couple days. There is a strong signal 
of a sharp cool down by the weekend. Frost may be possible as 
low temperatures plunge well into the 30s by Sunday morning.
